Innovation Game: A Summer School Applying Serious Game Design in Health Care and Education (iGame) is an EIT Health summer school at Uppsala University in Sweden that uses gamification as a tool to address real-life healthcare challenges to produce results that are beneficial to society.
Participants will gain skills in working in multidisciplinary teams and in cooperating with serious gaming experts and professionals from the business and public healthcare sector.
Solutions will be shared through outreach activities encouraging professionals to adopt an innovative mind-set to address health issues for children and adolescents.

EIT Health RIS activities focus on the following strategic areas of action in 2019: Mapping local innovation ecosystem in EIT RIS regions, identifying key players, unique assets and selling points as well as focus areas and investment needs.
Identifying connection points and synergies between regional capabilities and EIT Health strategic goals.

Bulle est une application web de soins de support à distance, unique en France, qui permet de réunir une équipe coordonnée autour de chaque patient atteint de cancer, de lui organiser un parcours personnalisé d’activités physiques et psycho-corporelles, et de consulter des professionnels à distance.
Le concept de Bulle est inédit en France : c’est un accompagnement humain qui s’appuie sur le digital afin que les patients puissent acquérir de l’autonomie dans la gestion de leur qualité de vie.
La plateforme est mise en oeuvre par Digital Pharma Lab, premier accélérateur PharmaTech indépendant en Europe.

Pas moins de six partenaires (Amgen, AstraZeneca, MSD, Pfizer, Servier et EIT Health) se sont donc alliés pour aider Bulle à accélérer son développement, suite à la première sélection de projets innovants de la Coalition Innovation Santé, le 10 avril 2020.

Bulle est soutenue par les plus grands Centres de Lutte Contre le Cancer : Gustave Roussy et l’Institut Curie à Paris, l’Institut Godinot à Reims, l’ICM à Montpellier, le Centre Antoine Lacassagne à Nice, le Centre Jean Perrin à Clermont-Ferrand, le Centre Léon Bérard à Lyon, le Centre Eugène Marquis à Rennes, l’Institut de Cancérologie de Lorraine et les Hôpitaux de Chartres.

Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur https://bulle.health À propos de la Coalition Innovation Santé La “Coalition Innovation Santé – Crise Sanitaire” a été créée sous l’impulsion de France Biotech, France Digitale, MedTech in France et l’entreprise biopharmaceutique AstraZeneca, avec les soutiens de l’AP-HP, Bpifrance, EIT Health.
En France, Amgen se consacre à faire progresser la prise en charge du cancer, des maladies cardiovasculaires, inflammatoires et rénales.
Ce dispositif, lancé à l’aube des 30 ans d’Amgen en France, s’inscrit dans un contexte politique en faveur du soutien à l’innovation et aux sciences de la vie.

En France, AstraZeneca rassemble plus de 1000 collaborateurs sur l’ensemble du territoire, notamment à son siège de Paris La Défense, son site industriel de Dunkerque et son site de conditionnement et de distribution de Reims.
EIT Health est un instrument Horizon 2020.
EIT Health est composé de 7 noeuds géographiques répartis sur toute l’Europe.
Cette communauté regroupe plus de 210 partenaires, industriels, académiques, clusters dans le domaine des MedTech, BioTech ou DigiTech.

Part of EIT Health Accelerator, Investor Network aims to connect European health-oriented investors with promising, pre-screened start-ups, so that ideas for improving healthcare can get into the market.

EIT Health Investor Network encourages cross-border financing and co-investment to facilitate fundraising that will help late-development-stage European start-ups conquer health markets faster and better.

It offers high-potential start-ups connections to a wide variety of private-equity investors, as well as coaching by seasoned investors and serial entrepreneurs and potential access to the EIT Health Living Labs network.

For private investors, business angel associations and representatives of venture capital or corporate venture funds, EIT Health Investor Network offers a great opportunity to review and select pre-screened innovative companies according to the properties of their portfolio – and to join a select network of investors.

How it works The ambitions of the Investor Network are to: Allow start-ups to access funding faster Foster earlier internationalization with cross-border investors Leverage local funding with international co-investments Investor Network will create a qualified deal-flow around a common platform, international gatherings, face-to-face meetings and online pitches.

Angels Santé, the largest Business Angels Association dedicated to healthcare, is leading a partnership with BIO Clustermanagement NRW GmbH and Imperial College Health Partners to build this unique cross-border investor community.
After an official 3 May 2018 kick-off in London, during the Global Investor Forum, the Network has held investors’ meetings in Milan, Lisbon, and Rotterdam.

Investors who wish to join the Investor Network are encouraged to contact operations@angelssante.fr or any of EIT Health’s Business Development Specialists located in various regional offices around Europe.

EIT Health Spain has launched in Barcelona the F 3 T – Framework for Fast Fast-Track of Digital Health Solutions project.

The initiative brings together experts and players in the health innovation value chain to define a framework to speed up the adoption of digital health applications in Spain, with implementable recommendations for decision-makers.

The ultimate goal is to reach a minimum consensus for harmonisation in the processes of evaluation, adoption and financing of digital health applications in Spain, as well as to facilitate the scalability of solutions .
The F 3 T is the result of consultations and meetings that EIT Health held in 2022 which are included in the report ‘Accelerating the adoption of digital health applications in Spain’ .
The report identifies the obstacles in the way of innovation in digital health apps and the areas where is key to intervene as a priority.

“In the future, high-quality and clinically validated mobile health apps will help to fill some gaps in healthcare, improve or even replace some conventional treatments, and help make healthcare systems more resilient and financially viable.

“But if we are not able to ensure that the best innovations in this field reach the patient and the system quickly, equitably and safely, we will be missing the opportunity provided by European and national transformation funds and plans,” says Izabel Alfany, Director of Operations at EIT Health Spain.

In this sense, the Core Group aspires to a common minimum harmonisation framework for all Autonomous Regions and healthcare organisations , avoiding ineffective repetition of pilots, which reduces the scalability of applications and equity in patient access to innovation.
Germany took the lead by launching a novel process for the fast-track approval of digital, prescribable and reimbursable apps (popularly known as DiGA fast-track ).
France, Belgium and Luxembourg are also moving in this direction.
“Spain cannot be left behind and needs a consensus of all the stakeholders so that the solutions that bring value for patients reach them as soon as possible and in a safe way.

As the main driving force in the health innovation ecosystem, at EIT Health we believe we have the responsibility and the capacity to facilitate this process,” said Ángeles Barrios, Public Affairs Lead at EIT Health Spain , who is responsible for coordinating the project.

Current landscape and roadmap” 19th April 2023 During 2022, EIT Health launched a series of roundtables in different European countries, with the aim of raising awareness and initiating a dialogue on the state of regulation of digital health applications and the changes needed to ensure that the best innovation reaches patients and citizens as soon as possible.
EIT Health Spain organised several debates on this topic and participated in different activities on a regional level.
The Spanish report The report ‘A ccelerating the adoption of digital health applications in Spain.

The different perspectives and inputs from the experts resulted in a 20-point roadmap to accelerate the adoption of innovative digital health applications that are truly transformative for the healthcare system, generate a thriving business network and, most importantly, deliver value to patients.

However, accelerating the adoption of transformative digital health applications and solutions requires a collaborative approach, with all players in the value chain at key points in the innovation process: Develop support tools for innovators in stages before CE certification.
Develop an appropriate regulatory process that balances the reality and regulations of health systems, the nature of digital solutions, protection, patient needs and the success of innovators.
Develop a set of clinical validation criteria – based on value – for digital applications and seek their harmonisation within Europe to support a true European health space and market.
Develop and pilot public procurement and funding models that enable startups and SMEs to develop beneficial digital health applications and access the service portfolio of public health systems.

The European report In the coming days, EIT Health will launch a report that addresses the state of play of the adoption of digital health devices and applications and the potential harmonisation of evaluation and access processes at the European level.

Call open Biotech Certified Innovation Path EIT Health invites organisations from industry, education and research to submit proposals for the development of a new EIT Label-certified Biotech pathway within the Certified Innovation Path (CIP) portfolio, complementing the existing Health Data, Digital Medical Devices and High Value Care pathways.
Funded projects will design and deliver personalised learning courses for graduates and professionals across the health biotechnology value chain.
The pathway will equip participants with the innovation, entrepreneurship and biotech expertise needed to translate scientific advances into scalable, market-ready healthcare solutions across Europe.

A consortium of minimum two Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) established in two different eligible Member States, of which: At least one HEI must be established in an EIT RIS region; and At least one of the participating Higher Education Institutions must be authorised to award ECTS credits for the repurposed courses.
Active and substantive involvement of non-academic or industry partners is essential, as a highly integrated, innovative learning by doing approach is a core principle of EIT Labelled Fellowships.

About the course Proposed courses must aim to: Equip participants to navigate and apply Europe’s evolving regulatory and policy landscape, including the EU Biotech Act, Clinical Trials Regulation and MDR/IVDR, with a focus on translation and early scaleup.
Integrate advanced biotech and translational expertise with EIT Labelled innovation, entrepreneurship and leadership competencies, enabling real-world implementation of biotech innovation.

Strengthen cross border collaboration, mobility and industry engagement, connecting European research, clinical, manufacturing and investment ecosystems through applied learning and capstone projects.

Call open Design and Deliver the Next EIT Health Bootcamps Help shape the next generation of EIT Health Bootcamps and unlock the market potential of Europe’s most promising health innovations.

We are looking for experienced consortia from across industry, education and research to design and deliver intensive, hands-on learning paths for health start-ups ready to advance their innovations towards market adoption and scale.

This opportunity is designed for organisations with expertise in healthcare innovation, entrepreneurship, commercialisation, education and venture support, and strong connections across the European health innovation ecosystem.

Bring your expertise to one or more of five learning paths covering foundational health innovation skills, digital health validation and evidence, deep tech and AI commercialisation, cross-border investment and scaling, and patient access and adoption.

Working alongside EIT Health, selected consortia will develop engaging learning experiences that combine practical training, expert-led masterclasses, tailored mentoring, real-world case studies, ecosystem engagement and pitch opportunities.

Equip participating start-ups with the knowledge, tools and connections to strengthen validation and evidence generation, navigate regulatory and market access pathways, build investment readiness, engage healthcare stakeholders and develop actionable strategies for market entry and scale.

Through expert guidance and connections with investors, healthcare providers, industry, regulators and patient communities, the Bootcamps will help ventures identify and overcome the barriers standing between promising innovation and real-world adoption.

Join EIT Health in building scalable learning programmes that strengthen Europe’s health innovation ecosystem and give health start-ups the capabilities, connections and confidence to take the next step towards commercialisation and impact.
This call is open to consortia with the expertise and capacity to design and deliver high-quality learning experiences for health start-ups.
Consortia must comprise a minimum of two and a maximum of five independent legal entities, with at least two entities legally established in different Horizon Europe countries.

Call open EIT Health RIS Country Representatives Become the driving force behind healthcare innovation in your country.
EIT Health is looking for ambitious organisations to become Country Representatives in selected EIT Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS) countries for 2027–2028.
As EIT Health’s national representative, you’ll play a central role in shaping the future of healthcare innovation by connecting the people, organisations and ideas that drive meaningful change.

Working across academia, research, healthcare, industry, start-ups, investors and public authorities, you’ll strengthen your country’s health innovation ecosystem and create new opportunities for collaboration through EIT Health’s innovation, education and business creation programmes.

As a Country Representative, you’ll identify and support promising innovators and entrepreneurs, build regional innovation capacity, promote EIT Health funding and programme opportunities, and help local organisations connect with one of Europe’s leading health innovation networks.

If your organisation has a strong regional network, proven experience in innovation ecosystem development, entrepreneurship support, technology transfer or healthcare innovation, and the ambition to make a lasting impact, this is your opportunity to become part of Europe’s largest health innovation community.
